product: bounds-ledger — a continuously re-verified ledger of drifting mathematical records
_disclosureNote: This repo is PUBLIC (since 2026-08-08), so this manifest is written for a public reader. It states the controls that ARE in place and names remaining gaps by tracker ID only. It deliberately does not enumerate our unprotected surfaces — publishing a weakness inventory was one of the eight blockers found by the 2026-08-05 pre-publication review, and the fix was not to write a better inventory but to stop publishing one.

runtime.framework: none — Node stdlib and global fetch only
runtime.dependencies: ZERO by design. package-lock.json is committed and CI installs with `npm ci`, so the empty dependency set is a ratchet rather than a coincidence: adding a package becomes a visible, reviewable diff.

deploy.note: Nothing deploys. There is no service, no runtime host and no build artifact — the repo IS the product, and the only automation is a scheduled GitHub Actions job that re-fetches the stewarded surfaces and fails when a cited record moves.

datastores.note: ledger/teorth-optimizationproblems/** is a byte-level mirror of the adopted upstream surface; ledger/claims.json holds the value pins; continuity/*.json holds the item ledger and traffic samples. No database.

authModel: none — no accounts, no sessions, no user data of any kind.

secrets.envFiles: none — this repo has no .env of any kind
secrets.repoSecrets: none. Deliberate and load-bearing: two local checks need a credential and BOTH are allowed to report unverified in CI rather than have a credential added to a public repo's Actions secrets. `check-brief.mjs` reads CC_PROMPTS_PIN from the operator's environment; `traffic-snapshot.mjs` delegates entirely to the `gh` CLI and never handles a token itself.
secrets.ciCredential: the ephemeral github.token issued per workflow run, used only to file a finding issue on drift

requiredChecks.enforcement: GitHub Actions on push to main, on a daily schedule, and on manual dispatch
requiredChecks.ci: 10 network-free self-tests, then the live mirror-drift check and the cross-surface claim check; a red run files a finding issue titled with what actually moved
preCommit: node scripts/history-sweep.mjs --staged — refuses a commit whose staged diff carries secret-shaped content
additional: reverify.test.mjs asserts every self-test in `npm test` has a workflow step, so a check cannot be added without CI coverage
reverify.test.mjs asserts every piped workflow step declares `shell: bash` — the runner default has no pipefail, and a piped check reports the pipe's exit code instead of its own

secretScanning.preCommit: present — core.hooksPath is set to .githooks and the hook runs the repo's own pattern set over the staged diff (2026-08-09)
secretScanning.verifiedHistorySweep: on-demand gate, not yet scheduled — scripts/history-sweep.mjs sweeps all reachable history and was run as the pre-publication gate; the scheduled control is fleet-owned and tracked as A-7

branchProtection.main: protected by repository ruleset `main-history-integrity` (id 20607202, enforcement active, no bypass actors): deletion and non-fast-forward pushes are both blocked
branchProtection.note: No required-review rule: this is a single-contributor repo and requiring pull requests would add friction without adding a reviewer. A deliberate history rewrite now requires disabling the ruleset first, which is the intended friction on an irreversible action.

errorMonitoring.note: Nothing runs as a service, so there is nothing to instrument. The drift job's own failures surface as GitHub issues, and an instrument failure is titled as such rather than as a record drift.

observability.driftAlarm: scheduled reverify job; a red run is the alarm, not a bug
observability.traffic: npm run traffic accumulates GitHub's 14-day traffic window into continuity/traffic.json (W-6)

knownGaps: W-5 — upstream's own README is outside the mirrored surface, so a record demoted from headline to asterisked is not yet visible to the drift alarm
